subject: DynamoHealth capacity crosswalk + cutover cadence (staging -> prod)
messages:
From: Elaine Summers <elaine@dynamohealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-08T14:23:00Z
Subject: Quick: sizing numbers & preferred cutover weekend

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to confirm a few concrete sizing knobs so they can greenlight the reserved capacity commitment: steady-state QPS we should expect, peak concurrency, and the preferred cutover weekend window.

High-level DynamoHealth constraints:
- Model: llama-70b-int8 (we're standardizing on this for parity)
- Expected steady-state: ~120 requests/min (chat-style, avg 650 tokens/request)
- Peak spikes: up to 350 requests/min for onboarding waves (short bursts ~10–15 minutes)
- Latency target: p95 < 350ms for 1- to 2-turn chats

Can your team propose a validated GPU count and a recommended cutover weekend (we have lower traffic on weekends of July 18–19 or July 25–26)? Also please attach any staging validation checklist we should run.

Regards,
Elaine
Senior Product Manager, DynamoHealth

P.S. procurement@dynamohealth.com is looped for timeline visibility.

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Summers <elaine@dynamohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-08T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick: sizing numbers & preferred cutover weekend

Elaine —

Thanks, this is perfect. I ran a quick back-of-envelope and attached a first-pass crosswalk. Short summary: to hit p95 <350ms with llama-70b-int8 using our optimized runtime, we recommend initial reserved capacity of 6 A100-equivalent cards behind the dedicated pool with the following configuration:

- 6 GPUs (A100 equiv) with 2 inference workers each -> ~12 workers
- Expected steady throughput: ~130 req/min comfortably with prefix caching
- Burst headroom: up to ~360 req/min for short bursts if we enable temporary burst nodes (autoscale + burst credits)
- Warm KV cache replication across 3 nodes for reduced cold-starts

I'll loop Ben and Karthik for throughput validation and the staging checklist. We can propose a staged cutover:
1) Staging validation week (July 12–16): stress tests, cache warm, perf regression checks
2) Dry-run swap (weekday evening July 16): mirrored traffic switch for 2 hours
3) Production cutover candidate: weekend July 25–26 (pref) with rollback window of 2 hours

Attachments: dynamo_capacity_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (contains assumptions & headroom model).

Quick ask: Elaine, can you share a sample traffic trace (1 day) or a synthetic ramp pattern so we can run realistic replay tests?

— Logan
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elaine Summers <elaine@dynamohealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick: sizing numbers & preferred cutover weekend

Looping in specifics from infra side. Notes from my perf runs against a 70B-int8 replica using our v2 runtime (latest kernels):
- Single A100-equivalent worker serves ~11 concurrent chat sessions at target latency p95=320ms (650 token avg).
- With 12 workers (6 GPUs x2) we get sustained 132 req/min at target SLAs.
- For short spikes to 350 req/min we need burst nodes: recommend 2 spare GPUs in a burst pool (pre-warmed) + conservative autoscale policy (scale-in hold = 7m).
- KV cache warming: we should push a 6-hour prefix warm job during staging to ensure >90% cache hit during cutover.

Risk callouts:
- Network egress throttles on DynamoHealth side caused +15–40ms jitter in internal tests — recommend we run the staging-network-diagram.pdf checks with Carlos (edgecloud) before swapping.
- Quantization variance: require eval run with customer prompts to catch any tail-case quality shifts.

Action items:
- Karthik: run replay on July 13 using their sample trace (pending).
- Marissa: coordinate dry-run monitoring dashboard and incident channel.

Ben
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Summers <elaine@dynamohealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Carlos Vega <carlos@edgecloud.io>
Date: 2026-07-10T16:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick: sizing numbers & preferred cutover weekend

Ben —

I kicked off a replay run using a synthetic ramp that mirrors DynamoHealth's onboarding spike pattern (burst to 350 req/min over 5 min, hold 15 min). Preliminary results attached in the Drive link; summary here:
- 6 GPU baseline with 2 burst GPUs achieved p95=340ms on median replay; tail occasionally hits ~370ms during cold cache windows.
- With a 6-hour warm job and 2 pre-warmed burst GPUs we consistently stay under 350ms.

Proposed change: bump baseline to 7 GPUs for the first 30 days and re-evaluate after traffic stabilization (this buys predictable headroom and reduces burst churn costs). Operational impact: incremental monthly reserved cost + one-time onboarding credit request.

Elaine/Carlos: can EdgeCloud confirm that the staging network tests (staging-network-diagram.pdf) will be scheduled for July 14? I want ingress/egress checks prior to replay.

Karthik
Perf Lead, Redwood Inference

From: procurement@dynamohealth.com
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Elaine Summers <elaine@dynamohealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T13:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Quick: sizing numbers & preferred cutover weekend

Hi team —

Procurement has reviewed the crosswalk. Two requests before final commit:
1) Can Redwood provide a 30-day SLA credit clause for performance regressions during the first month of go-live?
2) Please confirm rollback playbook and who owns cutover incident response — we need on-call names and escalation paths.

We would prefer the July 25–26 weekend. Please confirm and share the final MOP (method of procedures).

Thanks,
Procurement, DynamoHealth
procurement@dynamohealth.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@dynamohealth.com, Elaine Summers <elaine@dynamohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Carlos Vega <carlos@edgecloud.io>
Date: 2026-07-14T09:11:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick: sizing numbers & preferred cutover weekend

Procurement / Elaine —

We can accommodate the requests. Concrete commitments:
- SLA credit: Redwood will include a 30-day performance allowance clause for regressions tied to the cutover, capped at 10% of monthly committed fees; legal to follow with exact language (I will route this after internal sign-off).
- Cutover ownership & incident response: primary on-call (Redwood): Ben Carter (infra lead) for first-line mitigation; secondary: Karthik Iyer (perf lead); DynamoHealth on-call: Elaine Summers (PM) and DynamoHealth SRE (procurement has SRE contact list). Escalation path: Slack incident channel -> PagerDuty -> Exec notification.
- Final MOP & runbook: attached with this thread and pushed to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-dynamo-cutover.
- Scheduling: confirm staging validation July 13–16; dry-run July 16 evening; final cutover weekend July 25–26. We will provision 7 GPUs baseline for the first 30 days and maintain 2 pre-warmed burst GPUs.

Next steps for DynamoHealth: share traffic trace for replay by EOD July 12. For EdgeCloud/Carlos: please confirm network test slot on July 14.

Thanks — we’ll follow up with the MOP and the revised crosswalk that reflects the 7 GPU baseline.

— Logan
Director, Solutions, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192
